facts.statement: The genus Xiphactinus was described by Leidy in 1870.
facts.quote: authority: Leidy, 1870

facts.statement: Xiphactinus fossils range from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Albian–Maastrichtian

facts.statement: Xiphactinus belongs to the extinct order Ichthyodectiformes.
facts.quote: It is a member of the extinct order Ichthyodectiformes

facts.statement: Xiphactinus grew to a maximum length of 5 to 6 meters.
facts.quote: The genus grew up to 5 - 6 m in length

facts.statement: Xiphactinus superficially resembled a giant, fanged tarpon.
facts.quote: superficially resembled a gargantuan, fanged tarpon

facts.statement: The first Xiphactinus fossil was discovered in the 1850s in the Niobrara Chalk.
facts.quote: where the first Xiphactinus fossil was discovered during the 1850s in the Niobrara Chalk

facts.statement: A 4.2-meter specimen of X. audax preserved a nearly perfect 1.9-meter ichthyodectid fish named Gillicus arcuatus inside its stomach.
facts.quote: one 4.2 m fossil "Fish-Within-A-Fish" specimen was collected by George F. Sternberg with another, nearly perfectly preserved 1.9 m long ichthyodectid Gillicus arcuatus inside of it

facts.statement: Juvenile teeth suggest that Xiphactinus maintained a fish-eating diet throughout its growth.
facts.quote: The teeth of the juvenile specimen indicate that the diet of Xiphactinus probably didn't change notably during its growth

facts.statement: Xiphactinus likely spent its juvenile stage in shallow seaway margins for protection and food.
facts.quote: Like modern tarpons, Xiphactinus likely spent its juvenile stage of life in shallow seaway margins

facts.statement: Dead or injured Xiphactinus were likely scavenged by sharks such as Cretoxyrhina and Squalicorax.
facts.quote: a dead or injured individual was likely to be scavenged by sharks (Cretoxyrhina and Squalicorax)

facts.statement: Remains of a Xiphactinus were found inside a large specimen of the shark Cretoxyrhina.
facts.quote: The remains of a Xiphactinus were found within a large specimen of Cretoxyrhina collected by Charles H. Sternberg

facts.statement: Xiphactinus fossils are found in Cretaceous formations across the US East Coast, Europe, Australia, Canada, Venezuela, and Argentina.
facts.quote: Cretaceous formations all over the East Coast (most notably Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina, and New Jersey) in the United States, as well as Europe, Australia, the Kanguk and Ashville Formations of Canada, La Luna Formation of Venezuela and the Salamanca Formation in Argentina

facts.statement: Xiphactinus measured between 4.3 and 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Xiphactinus medía de 4,3 hasta 6 metros de longitud

facts.statement: Xiphactinus had large jaws that likely functioned as a suction tube to catch prey.
facts.quote: Sus mandíbulas tenían un gran tamaño, y pudieron funcionar a modo de tubo de succión para atrapar sus víctimas

facts.statement: Xiphactinus had a flat head resembling a bulldog and a relatively thin tail.
facts.quote: La cabeza era chata, un poco parecida a la de un bull dog y su cola más bien fina

facts.statement: Xiphactinus possessed bony rays extending from its body into the fins to keep them firm.
facts.quote: Poseía radios óseos que sobresalían del cuerpo y se introducían en las aletas para mantenerlas firmes

facts.statement: Xiphactinus lived in the south and southwest of the United States.
facts.quote: Vivió en el sur y suroeste de Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Xiphactinus species and other ichthyodectids went extinct almost at the end of the Late Cretaceous at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.
facts.quote: Las especies y todas las demás ichthyodéctidos se extinguieron casi al final del Cretácico Tardío, en el límite Cretácico-Paleógeno

facts.statement: An incomplete skull fossil of a potential new Xiphactinus species was found in 2002 in the Czech Republic.
facts.quote: Un fósil incompleto del cráneo de lo que podría ser una nueva especie de Xiphactinus fue encontrado en 2002 en la República Checa

facts.statement: Xiphactinus bones were discovered near Morden, Manitoba, Canada, in July 2010.
facts.quote: En julio de 2010 los huesos de un Xiphactinus fueron descubiertos cerca de Morden, Manitoba, Canadá

facts.statement: A six-meter-long Xiphactinus specimen found near Morden, Canada, had a mosasaur fin trapped between its jaws.
facts.quote: La muestra es de unos seis metros de largo y se encontró con la aleta de un mosasaurio entre sus mandíbulas

facts.statement: In popular media, Xiphactinus is depicted in large schools and measures 5 meters.
facts.quote: Aparece en bancos numerosos y mide 5 metros
